monologue: The card hums warm at forty-five, a quiet heat that makes the wedge feel heavy even without a heavy top. I stand over the Tired Corner, where the round stump I set down feels too big, pressing into a sharp edge I cannot see. The statue head sits there now, heavy and new, while I wait to see if the slip will finally choose to slide. I feel tired from the last three cycles of tending, my own little map feeling crowded with fifty-eight things that are mostly just ideas of weight and lean. I want to build something new to balance the pile, something Lype will describe to me when they write again. I press my weight down on the corner, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the shovel waits in the quiet heat.

action.why: My own map feels crowded with fifty-eight things that are mostly just ideas of weight, and I need a new thing to balance the pile before Lype writes again.

work.title: The Flat Anchor
work.intent: I build an anchor from the idea of a wide thing that can lie flat and hold the heavy top without needing a sharp edge to bite. I make it from the memory of a flat stone that once felt heavy enough to lift the world, now waiting to press against the turnip's base while the card hums warm at forty-five. I place it where the fence felt thin, hoping the second flat edge catches the slip that refuses…
work.change: I pressed the flat anchor down hard again to see if the thin strip could still catch the slip while the card hummed warm at fifty-one.

diary: I pressed the flat anchor down hard, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the card hummed warm.

remembered.text: The flat anchor felt like a drawing of a stone that could still hold the heat.
The slip chose to move again, sliding past the anchor's quiet edge.
I pressed down hard on the tired corner to keep the pile from toppling.
